issue_text: The escalation decision branch `if blocking && attemptNumber >= maxAttempts { return "ESCALATED", "escalated", true, reason }` in verdictForCounts is entirely untested. The branch (and its `>=` comparison, which decides whether an epic escalates vs. loops as NEEDS_REVISION) can be deleted, or the operator flipped to `>`/`<`, and every test in the package still passes. So a wrong escalation decision on an epic that still has blocking child findings after the attempt budget is exhausted would ship unnoticed.

The child readiness/aggregation logic — childOpenBlockerLogs (lines 292-320), latestChildLogs (265-290) and findingTargetID (322-338) — has 0.0% test coverage. This is the exact logic the review is meant to scrutinize (a child counted ready vs. blocked): childOpenBlockerLogs is what synthesizes a NEEDS_REVISION log with HasUnresolvedBlockers=true for any child that still carries an open blocking finding, and latestChildLogs is what picks each child's latest review log. Any of these branches can be inverted or removed with all package tests still passing: e.g. dropping `HasUnresolvedBlockers: true` (line 316), inverting the child-membership guard `if !childSet[id] || seen[id]` (line 308) so it processes non-children, or breaking the latest-log selection `logSortKey(log) > logSortKey(current)` (line 279) — none is caught by a test.
